item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
A rectangular shaped swimming pool has a paved walkway around it as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a pool and walkway]

What is the area of the paved walkway?
item.figure_description: A diagram shows an outer shaded rectangle labeled "Walkway" surrounding an unshaded inner rectangle labeled "Pool". The dimensions of the outer rectangle are labeled with double-headed arrows: a length of 70 m along the top and a width of 23 m along the right side. The dimensions of the inner rectangle are also labeled with double-headed arrows: a length of 50 m along its top edge and a width of 18 m along its right edge.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A rectangular garden that is next to a building has a path around the other three sides, as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a garden and path next to a building]

What is the area of the path?
reference_items.figure_description: A diagram shows a thick line labeled "Building" forming a vertical wall. Directly adjacent to the building wall is a shaded rectangular "Garden", surrounded on the remaining three sides by an unshaded "Path" forming a larger outer rectangle. The dimensions shown are: total vertical height of the outer rectangle along the building wall is 12 m; horizontal length of the garden is 10 m; vertical height of the garden is 8 m; and total horizontal width of the outer rectangle (garden plus path width) along the bottom is 12 m.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Shaded rectangular diagram that is x meters by x plus 4 meters. A white, width-wise rectangular path goes down the middle of the diagram and is 1 meter by x meters.]

This is a diagram of a rectangular garden.

The white area is a rectangular path that is 1 meter wide.

Which expression shows the area of the shaded portion of the garden in m^2?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle with height labeled x m and total width labeled (x + 4) m. The rectangle is divided vertically into three sections: a shaded gray rectangular region on the left, a vertical white rectangular strip labeled "path" in the middle, and another shaded gray rectangular region on the right. An arrow beneath the white path indicates its width is 1 m.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: L-shaped polygon]

What is the area, in square cm, of the figure shown above?
reference_items.figure_description: An L-shaped polygon with six sides. The leftmost vertical side is labeled 8 cm. The bottom horizontal side is labeled 12 cm. From the top-left vertex, a horizontal top edge extends to the right to meet a vertical segment that goes downward, labeled 3 cm. From the bottom of that 3 cm segment, a horizontal edge labeled 9 cm extends to the right to meet the rightmost vertical side. Right-angle symbols are marked at five vertices: the top-left vertex, the vertex where the top horizontal edge meets the 3 cm vertical segment, the vertex where the 9 cm segment meets the right vertical side, the bottom-right vertex, and the bottom-left vertex.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle ABCD containing two tangent circles P and Q]

In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle, and circles P and Q each have a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the rectangle?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle ABCD is oriented horizontally with vertices labeled A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, and D at the bottom-left. Inside the rectangle are two identical circles labeled P and Q, with their centers marked by dots labeled P and Q. The two circles are tangent to each other horizontally at the midline of the rectangle. Circle P touches the left side AD, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. Circle Q touches circle P, the right side BC, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. A vertical line segment is drawn from center P up to the point of tangency on top side AB, labeled "5 cm".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Net of a rectangular box]

When the shape shown above is folded up, it will make a rectangular box.
What is the volume of the box?

Answer: ____ cm^3

descriptors: Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
A net of an open or closed rectangular box consisting of six rectangular faces:
- A central rectangle.
- A top flap attached to the top edge of the central rectangle, with width labeled 5 cm (indicated by a curly brace at the top) and height labeled 2 cm (indicated by a curly brace on its right side). The top-left and top-right corners have square right-angle markers.
- A bottom flap attached to the bottom edge of the central rectangle, with height labeled 2 cm (indicated by a curly brace on its right side). The bottom-left and bottom-right corners have square right-angle markers.
- A left flap attached to the left edge of the central rectangle, with width labeled 2 cm (indicated by a curly brace at the top). The top-left and bottom-left corners have square right-angle markers.
- Extending to the right from the central rectangle is a horizontal strip divided into two rectangles: the first rectangle is adjacent to the central rectangle, and the second (rightmost) rectangle has its width labeled 5 cm (indicated by a curly brace at the bottom) and its height labeled 3 cm (indicated by a curly brace on its right edge). The top-right and bottom-right corners of the rightmost rectangle have square right-angle markers.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A machine has 100 candies and dispenses a candy when a lever is turned. The machine has the same number of blue, pink, yellow, and green candies all mixed together. Megan turned the lever and obtained a pink candy. Peter turned the lever next.

How likely is it that Peter will get a pink candy?

options.label: A
options.text: It is certain that his candy will be pink.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely than it was for Megan.

options.label: C
options.text: It is exactly as likely as it was for Megan.

options.label: D
options.text: It is less likely than it was for Megan.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: A shaded rectangle that is 6 cm by 16 cm. Part of the rectangle is unshaded. The unshaded part of the rectangle forms a right triangle on the left that is 6 centimeters by 8 centimeters.]

In the figure above, what is the area of the shaded region in cm^2?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle with a height of 6 cm and a total length of 16 cm along the top, both labeled with dimension arrows. An unshaded right triangle occupies the bottom-left portion of the rectangle; its vertical leg is the left side of the rectangle (6 cm) and its horizontal leg along the bottom has a length of 8 cm labeled with a dimension arrow. The remainder of the rectangle is shaded solid black.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
